## Parent

Epic `77e3-28e2-31ec-47ec`, authorized at full scope by the operator on 2026-11-02.
This is deliverable 2. Depends on `fe94-2e22-ea9e-46f7`, which establishes the
net-mechanism criterion this story's own change must satisfy.

## The gap

A mechanism admitted by a `# mechanism-ok:` marker is admitted FOREVER. Measured at
`origin/main` `4cf1ae42946`:

- The marker grammar is `scripts/_mechanism_delta/markers.py:20` (`_MARKER_RE`), separators
  at `markers.py:23` — `("—", "--", "-", ":")` — and the capture at `markers.py:42-43`. It
  has exactly three fields: kind, name, reason. The reason is free text.
- `scripts/_mechanism_delta/compare.py:89-92` admits a `new` key when the marker's reason is
  nonblank. `compare.py:83` makes a blank reason an error.
- Nothing parses a ticket id out of the reason. Nothing checks that a referenced ticket
  exists, is open, or ever closes.

So an agent writes `# mechanism-ok: env_var REBAR_X — temporary, remove after the migration`
and the mechanism is permanently blessed. The migration closes; the marker stays; the
ratchet never looks again. The admission is a one-way door with no expiry.

## The change

Two halves.

**Half 1 — the marker names a sunset ticket.** Narrow the admission grammar so the third
field is a resolvable rebar ticket id rather than arbitrary prose. A marker whose third
field does not resolve is not an admission, and the ratchet fails as it would for a blank
reason.

**Half 2 — that ticket cannot close while the marker remains.** Add a deterministic
precheck to the completion-verification close path: when the ticket being closed is named
as the sunset ticket of a `# mechanism-ok:` marker still present in the tree, the close is
refused and the refusal names the marker's file and line.

## What this retires

Required by `fe94`'s net-mechanism criterion, which this story is the first change to be
judged by.

This change ADDS one deterministic close precheck. It RETIRES the free-text reason as an
accepted admission: after this change the only thing that admits a new mechanism is a
resolvable ticket id, so the "write any sentence and pass" path at `compare.py:89-92`
ceases to exist. The admission surface narrows rather than grows — one admission form
replaces one admission form, plus the enforcement that makes the new form mean something.

## Where the close refusal goes

The close gate has NO pluggable deterministic check — measured, not assumed. There is no
`_PRECHECKS` tuple and no registry of precheck callables in
`src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py`. Unlike plan review, which has
`det_invariants.run_project_det_checks` driven by `exec: "DET"` overlay entries, the close
path has no project-pluggable equivalent.

The seam is the straight-line call sequence inside `_completion_precheck`, which runs its
refusal points in order BEFORE the LLM verifier is invoked at `close_precheck.py:694`. The
existing landing check is `close_precheck.py:151` `_check_work_landed`, called at
`close_precheck.py:685`, raising at `close_precheck.py:215-222`. A new refusal is one more
call in that sequence and needs no restructuring.

Precedent that a precheck may read repository state beyond git history:
`close_precheck.py:289` `_check_file_impact_vs_diff` reads landed commits' diffs. The
sunset scan reads tracked file contents, which is a wider read than any existing precheck
performs, so the plan must state that explicitly rather than let review infer it.

## The --force caveat, stated rather than hidden

`close_precheck.py:634-637` short-circuits the ENTIRE precheck block via
`_gate_skip_expectation` when `--force="<reason>"` is passed. No deterministic close
refusal in this gate is unconditional, and this one will not be either. The acceptance
criteria below are therefore worded as refusal absent a human override, not as an absolute
bar. Per AGENTS.md agents must not use `--force`; the override is a human operator's
judgement call and is audited by the absence of a signed attestation.

## Portability

Per the blocking `project.portability` criterion, a check whose only trigger is a specific
CI system is not portable. Half 2 runs in-process in the close path with no CI dependency,
so it fires in any environment that can close a ticket. Half 1 runs inside
`scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py`, which `make lint` invokes locally and which CI also
invokes; its trigger is the lint target, not a CI provider, so it fires with no CI present.

## Provider neutrality

Both halves are deterministic. Neither calls an LLM, so there is no provider or model
dependency to be neutral about. This must be stated in the plan so review does not assume
an LLM path.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A `# mechanism-ok:` marker whose third field is not a resolvable ticket id does not
      admit its mechanism: `scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check` exits non-zero for a
      new mechanism carrying such a marker. Verified by a test.
- [ ] A marker whose third field IS a resolvable ticket id admits its mechanism and
      `--check` exits zero. Verified by a test.
- [ ] Closing a ticket named as the sunset ticket of a marker still present in the tree is
      refused, and the error names the marker's file and line. Verified by a test.
- [ ] Closing that same ticket succeeds once the marker is removed from the tree. Verified
      by a test.
- [ ] Closing a ticket named by NO marker is unaffected — the new precheck does not fire.
      Verified by a test.
- [ ] Removing a mechanism still passes the ratchet. Verified by a test, guarding the
      shrink-only asymmetry at `compare.py:99` where `counters.stale` is never consulted.
- [ ] Every existing marker in the tree is migrated to the new grammar, and
      `make lint` passes. Verified by `make verify`.
- [ ] The new precheck fires with no CI provider present. Verified by a test that
      exercises it with no CI environment configured.
- [ ] `make verify` passes.

## Open item for implementation

The count of `# mechanism-ok:` markers currently in the tree is not yet measured. The
migration in AC 7 is sized by that count, and it will be measured and recorded here before
plan review is requested.

## Measurement base

Every citation above was read from `origin/main` at `4cf1ae42946`. Line numbers are from
that commit.
